to certain specified types of “Covered Businesses,” including “perfume stores,” in a
“Covered Geographic Area” that encompassed A&S’s Fine Fragrance location at 501
East Olympic Boulevard.13

or two or more related transactions in a 24-hour period, to report such transactions
electronically to FinCEN.14 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO was effective from
October 9, 2014 through April 6, 2015.

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324 — Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: Neutral: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but the facts do not show transactions near the $10,000 CTR threshold, aggregation to exceed it, or intent to evade reporting.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements. To apply, the facts must support that the person (i) structured/assisted in structuring or attempted to do so, (ii) in connection with a domestic financial institution transaction, (iii) for the purpose of evading a reporting requirement under 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) (CTR reporting) or related provisions. Here, the listed cash transactions are ATM withdrawals of $215.77–$730.55 and one wire of $4,795; none are near the typical $10,000 CTR trigger and there is no indication of multiple same-day cash transactions being split to avoid a report that otherwise would have been required. The fact pattern also lacks evidence of purpose/intent to evade reporting (e.g., statements, patterns of deposits/withdrawals just under $10,000, or bank actions indicating a report would have been filed). Because the elements of structuring tied to an otherwise-reportable transaction and the requisite intent are not established, applicability of 31 U.S.C. § 5324 cannot be determined from these facts.
